Extreme weather before each interview, in one call

Source: R/wrappers.R
weather_extremes.Rd

Runs the whole chain from a survey and a daily climate raster to one row per household and lag: the number of days beyond thresholds or percentiles, the excess over them, and the spells they form, over the window before each interview. The result's c4e_history() shows the equivalent step-by-step code, to copy and adapt.

Usage

weather_extremes(
  survey,
  climate,
  lat = NULL,
  lon = NULL,
  id = NULL,
  interview = NULL,
  preset = NULL,
  above = NULL,
  below = NULL,
  p = NULL,
  spells = TRUE,
  min_spell = NULL,
  window = NULL,
  boundaries = NULL,
  baseline = NULL,
  unit = NULL,
  control = extremes_control()
)

Arguments

survey

The survey: a data frame with coordinates, a household identifier and interview dates, or a table from prepare_coord(); or a named list of them.

climate

A daily raster (file path or SpatRaster), or a table already extracted at the survey locations.

lat, lon, id, interview

<tidy-select> Survey columns: coordinates (found by name when left out), household identifier and interview date. Not needed after prepare_coord().

preset

Name of a preset, e.g. "heat" or "wet_days_p95".

above, below

Absolute thresholds, in the data's unit.

p

Probabilities for relative thresholds, e.g. c(0.9, 0.95).

spells

When TRUE, add spells of the flagged days.

min_spell

Minimum spell length in days; default 2.

window

The reference window; default the year before the interview, see window_lag().

boundaries

Optional administrative divisions: indicators are then computed per cell and averaged per division (area shares).

baseline

Optional dates c(from, to) for the percentiles.

unit

Unit of the thresholds, when the data's should not be used.

control

Further options, see extremes_control().

Value

A c4e_tbl with one row per household and lag; with keep_steps, a list of the intermediate tables; with dry_run, NULL.

Details

The chain: prepare_coord(), georef_coord(), read_climate(), extract_by_coord() (or extract_cell_by_poly() and aggregate_to_adm() with boundaries), convert_unit() when needed, calc_threshold_day() and/or calc_percentile() with calc_percentile_day() (or calc_heatwave()), calc_spell(), and summarise_by_interview().

Pick the indicators with a preset (see list_presets()) or with above, below and p; explicit arguments override the preset. Thresholds are read in the data's unit, except that Kelvin data with thresholds below 100 are converted to Celsius, and precipitation in metres to millimetres, with a message. Percentiles of precipitation leave out days below 0.1 mm unless control says otherwise.

survey may be a named list of surveys (waves, countries); each is processed in turn and the results are stacked with a survey column.

See also

climate_indices(), list_presets(), write_stata()

Examples

survey <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "survey.csv", package = "c4e"))
survey$interview <- as.Date(survey$interview)

weather_extremes(survey,
                 system.file("extdata", "tmax_daily.tif", package = "c4e"),
                 id = hhid, interview = interview, preset = "heat")
#> Using lat as `lat`.
#> Using lon as `lon`.
#> Taking the coordinates as longitude and latitude in "EPSG:4326"; give `crs`
#> otherwise.
#> Read tmax_daily: tmax [K], daily, 2021-01-01 to 2023-12-31, 1095 layers
#> (synthetic).
#> ℹ weather_extremes (heat): tmax in K, daily, 2021-01-01 to 2023-12-31
